Pied-à-terre tax · Class 1 Houses

Townhouses and 1–3 family houses over $5 million

Aggregate FY2027 counts across 6,802 Class 1 homes valued at $5 million or more, with brackets and the March 15 Form TC107 deadline.

Unlike condos and co-ops, one-, two-, and three-family houses in Tax Class 1 face a higher $5 million city market-value threshold and lower rates starting at 0.8%. Because Class 1 homes are valued by DOF near comparable house sales rather than rental income under RPTL § 581, city market values sit much closer to open-market prices (median 105.5% of sale price in our linked sales study).

Check any 1–3 family house: Search your street address or 10-digit BBL on the free NYC pied-à-terre checker → to see its FY2027 city market value, bracket, and Form TC107 deadline, or inspect a Sample $79 Assessment Report PDF.

Class 1 surcharge brackets (over $5 million)

  • $5 million to $15 million: 0.8% of total city market value ($40,000+ a year if non-primary).
  • Over $15 million to $25 million: 1.05% of total city market value.
  • Over $25 million: 1.3% of total city market value.

As with apartments, primary residences of the owner, qualifying relatives, or a 1-year arm's-length tenant are exempt (full exemption rules).

Class 1 deadline: March 15, 2027

To challenge a Class 1 house's FY2027 city market value behind the surcharge, file paper Form TC107 by March 15, 2027 (two weeks after the March 1 condo/co-op cutoff). See the TC107 guide and full 2027 calendar.
